unit.why: A single narrative: a tsaddik shuts himself in with his dying daughter Hinda, she dies, and on Sukkot night he reveals that he had meant to revive her like Elisha but his deceased father-in-law warned him off.

stories.start_quote: בעת שהיתה בתו הצדיקת מ׳ הינדא
stories.summary_en: When his righteous daughter Hinda lay dying, the tsaddik shut himself in alone with her on Shabbat, and she died that day. Only on the first night of Sukkot did he tell, in Yiddish, that he had wanted to revive her as Elisha revived the child, but his late father-in-law came and warned him that this was dangerous.
